title: Chapter 1133
paragraphs: Chapter 1133
Episode 259. The Truth of the World, Your Truth, My Truth (2)
Choice.
Normally, when a god chooses a human, it means forming a contract with them. But now, Valeria was using the word in a different sense.
"The person Solderet chose to stand against the Demon Army was not you, but Temar Runcandel."
Jin found those words strange.
It wasn't the part about him not being chosen from the beginning, but the part about 'standing against the Demon Army' that was strange.
"If he chose Temar to stand against the Demon Army, did Solderet know about the existence of the multiverse a thousand years ago?"
"No, he didn't know then either."
"How can he think of fighting them if he didn't even know of the Demon Army's existence? That story doesn't add up."
At those words, Valeria was silent for a long while.

"...You're right, it doesn't make sense. I also thought for a very long time about where to start and how to explain everything we did when I met you. But I concluded that it's impossible to fully explain all those paradoxes. So, I'm just going to transfer my memories to you directly."
"Your memories?"
"It'll be better that way since you have to go back as soon as possible anyway. It's not a situation where I can tell the whole long story either."
"Right, I have to get the power and go back even one second faster. To save the people who are left. The time here and outside flows differently, right?"
"Probably. It could be faster, or slower. But it might flow the same."
"You don't know? Didn't you say that you and Solderet prepared this legacy together?"
Jin answered in a sharp voice without realizing it.
Outside, the world was heading towards ruin, and people were being trampled and killed by Kelliark. He had come here after seeing those countless deaths with his own two eyes.
But she didn't know? Beings who could 'design' the future didn't even know that? Something was welling up inside him.
It was true that he had reached this place without dying thanks to Valeria showing him the way and stopping time.
But Jin was feeling a fundamental disappointment. He also felt a sense of futility. According to Valeria's words, Temar and he were no different from puppets of beings who could deduce the future.
It meant that not only their own but the entire world's fate was decided by their choices. People were living according to Solderet and Valeria's design without knowing anything.
Some fall fighting the Demon Army, and some drown in the red sea that has suddenly flooded the entire world. That was the outside world Jin had experienced until just now.
That's why he wanted to question her. Wasn't there a better design than this? Was this really the best they could do? An endless despair was still continuing outside.

"The one who made me regress must have been a joint decision between you and Solderet. Before I regressed... hah, the world wasn't like this then. It was better than this. At least until 1808, people could live without experiencing the world's destruction. Even if the Demon Army had invaded here in 1808, everyone could have lived until then."
Obtain the power left by Solderet and take revenge on Kelliark.

That was something he had to accomplish no matter what. But after that? If he just finished off Kelliark and the Demon Army, could the people who were definitely alive until 1808 before his regression still be alive? Could the already destroyed world return to how it was then? An unshakable question was piercing Jin's inner self.
"Yes... it was."
He couldn't see the face of Valeria on his back. But Jin felt he knew what kind of look Valeria had. It would be a devastated expression.

"Solderet... this legacy that you and he prepared. Can it resurrect the dead? Can it compensate for the suffering they experienced due to my regression, and can it restore the world to before it was destroyed...?"
Valeria bit her lip.
"That's impossible."
At Valeria's answer, Jin once again felt anger boiling inside him. But it was not an emotion directed at Solderet and Valeria.
That anger was directed at himself.
It was directed at his own incompetence.

"...I'm sorry. I was being shameless. You two must have tried harder than me to somehow avoid the worst-case scenario. It's not like you made someone like me regress because you wanted to toy with the world as you pleased, like the Zipples."
He wasn't being sarcastic. It wasn't easy to endure the boiling self-loathing. He shouldn't blame Solderet and Valeria, but himself for not doing better.

"We are the ones who are sorry. But what's important now is for you to quickly receive the power Solderet left behind and defeat Kelliark. If you keep going, a gate will appear. It must be painful to move slowly because of me, but please bear with it for a little longer. To open that gate, I need to be alive until then."
She had only recovered enough energy to be able to talk by absorbing Jin's magic; Valeria was, in fact, so deeply wounded that it wouldn't be strange if she stopped breathing at any moment.
"I'll go in a way that doesn't strain you as much as possible."
"At this speed, it'll probably take about ten minutes. I'll be shaping the memories to transfer to you until then."
"Alright..."
"Jin."
Valeria wrapped her arms more tightly around Jin's chest and buried her face in his shoulder.
"Yeah."
"The future is unknown. It can't be confirmed perfectly with anything. The ending... no one can know it beforehand."
Valeria knew the outside situation well, too. The fact that the world had been irreversibly destroyed, the fact that even the light of regeneration Jin had spread had all been extinguished.
'Even if the dead can't return, at the very least, I hope there is land left for Jin and the remaining people to stand on... I truly hope so.'
She could only hope that if Jin defeated Kelliark, there would be a better ending than that.

"So even if you get Solderet's power, don't let your guard down, and even if you defeat him, don't think that the world is already over. The same goes for if you lose by any chance. You'll surely be like that even if I don't advise you, but still, I just wanted to say it."
"Thank you."
Wooooong...!
A ball of blue light formed above Valeria's head. Jin silently moved forward on the dark path, looking at that light.
Suddenly, he remembered the time he had spent with Valeria before his regression.

Their relationship had started as master and apprentice, but from some point on, they would lie down together and fall asleep at night. No one had ever said, we are lovers, but the people they happened to meet all saw them as lovers.
Remembering before his regression, that was the best time. Until his sudden death in Akin, Jin had believed that there would be more happiness than pain left in his life.

"Come to think of it, the fact that you and Solderet disappeared before I died must also be related to this legacy. Solderet... did he disappear because he was making me regress? Or did he disappear while trying to preserve the power to give to me here? Or is he alive beyond that gate? I have too many questions."
He knew no answer would come. Valeria was entering a state of concentration so deep that she was completely blocking out external stimuli.

"I'll find out everything when your memories are transferred anyway. How's the outside world? I really hope time is flowing more slowly here. I hope no one else has died when I get out. It'll be like that, right?"
Churururuk-!
Suddenly, the blood that had flowed from Valeria's abdomen poured onto the floor. Startled, Jin stopped in his tracks and checked her pulse. Fortunately, her breathing was stable.
But Valeria would die in the end. Jin knew that she was only postponing her death using sealing magic.
"...No, as you said, the future is unknown. You can live too, Valeria. I don't want to lose you again today. We'll be leaving together once I get the power anyway. Let's go to Lani then."
Lani is... alive, right?
Like a sea that never ends no matter how much you bail it out, the terrible thoughts just wouldn't stop. The more they came, the more Jin stared forward with force in his eyes.
It was really soon now. The power to tear Kelliark apart was waiting for him at the end of this desolate road.
Ten minutes felt like ten years.
Still, it seemed the path was almost at its end. The scenery, which had been just dark, was slowly changing.
It was getting brighter.
"Light...?"
As if a light had suddenly bloomed in a cave, after a few more steps, the surroundings suddenly became completely bright.
He reflexively looked back. But the endless darkness that had been spread out until just a moment ago was gone without a trace. The entire subspace had begun to shine brilliantly.
Looking in the direction he had been going again, he saw a huge white gate standing tall about a hundred paces ahead. If there was an ore made of condensed light, it seemed to be a gate made of that.
"Valeria, I think we're here."
"I just finished too, Jin. I'll open the gate now."
As Valeria waved her hand in the air, a blue window opened in front of the two. Following her hand, the familiar Hister cipher was being written on the window.
Jin could read that cipher. Valeria let out a chuckle.
"It's a bit cliché. I'd feel burdened if I were you."
Clunk-! Drrrrrrrk...!
The white gate was parting to both sides. The inside was again filled with darkness, and nothing could be seen.
"Let's go in now. And here, take this."
Valeria held out a blue orb, a little larger than her fist, in front of Jin's face. It was the memories she had been forming with her magic until just now.
"If you hold this, my memories will be transferred to you..."
The moment Valeria said that, Jin hastily drew his sword and turned around.
Tzaaang-!
"Kuhk!"
A sword energy had suddenly flown in from behind. It was the direction the two had just come from. Jin's balance was broken by the impact, and Valeria fell from Jin's back, spitting out blood.
"Jin!"
Valeria shouted Jin's name, her face pale. She had a gut feeling about who had attacked them just now.
She was sure. She didn't know how she had gotten in, but it was definitely Silyn Zipple.
"Silyn Zipple, how did you...!"
"Leader of the rebels, Valeria Hister. It seems you were in a hurry. You don't seem to have thought that I let you go on purpose in the dimensional passage."
Silyn Zipple.
As far as Valeria knew, she was an opponent Jin could never handle in his current state.
"Jin, hurry, go!"
Silyn was already extending her sword towards Jin's forehead and speaking thus.
"As if I'd let that happen."
